question: Can delayed generalization arise because a neural network first fits with its initial kernel and only later learns task-aligned features, even without weight decay or an adaptive optimizer?

key_findings.claim: The paper constructs clean counterexamples to explanations that require decreasing parameter norm, weight decay, or adaptive-optimizer instability.
key_findings.evidence: A two-layer MLP on modular arithmetic and a committee machine on polynomial regression grok under vanilla gradient descent, zero explicit regularization, and increasing weight norm. Thus those ingredients can amplify but are not necessary for delayed loss generalization.

key_findings.claim: In the analyzable polynomial example, early behavior follows the initial-NTK solution and late behavior aligns learned features with the quadratic teacher.
key_findings.evidence: The network output and kernel reduce to the first two weight moments. An exact population-MSE decomposition separates variance, target-matrix misalignment, and unwanted linear-mode power; during the delay, the model first loads linear kernel modes, then its second moment rotates toward the teacher and test loss falls.

key_findings.claim: Output scale and initial kernel-target alignment independently control the delay in the toy setting.
key_findings.evidence: Increasing output multiplier alpha slows relative feature movement and lengthens the train-test loss gap, approaching fixed-kernel regression; decreasing quadratic coefficient epsilon makes the target less represented by high-eigenvalue NTK modes and increases required feature learning. A phase diagram shows strongest grokking when training is initially lazy and misaligned.

key_findings.claim: A Goldilocks sample regime is required: enough data for learned features to generalize, but not enough for training and test loss to track immediately.
key_findings.evidence: Initial-kernel learning of a degree-k polynomial can require dimension-to-the-k samples while feature learning can need far fewer; appendix sweeps show no successful generalization at too little data and little delay at abundant data. Labels chosen from intermediate NTK eigenvectors also synthetically induce a delay.

key_findings.claim: MNIST, transformer, and student-teacher experiments show alpha controls the phenotype, but do not prove that every grokking mechanism is a lazy-to-rich transition.
key_findings.evidence: Rescaling output continuously weakens or strengthens delayed curves in an MNIST MLP, Nanda et al.'s one-layer modular-addition transformer under AdamW/cross-entropy, and a student-teacher network. The paper does not directly quantify NTK drift, feature-alignment causality, or optimizer dynamics in those broader cases and explicitly lacks sharp transition-time theory.

method.core_idea: Model grokking as timescale separation between fast fitting by nearly fixed initialization features and slow task-driven feature learning that later improves generalization.
method.mechanism: Use an output scale alpha to tune the parameterization from rich to lazy without changing the target, and use NTK-target centered alignment or a toy coefficient epsilon to tune how inadequate initial features are. In a two-layer quadratic committee machine, express prediction, NTK, and population error through mean and second-moment sufficient statistics; monitor their transition under full-batch GD. Sweep sample size and replicate alpha control in broader architectures.
assumptions: Early training is well approximated by the network linearization and its initialization NTK.
Centered kernel alignment captures how much useful target structure lies in easily learned initial modes.
Late feature learning reaches a better-generalizing representation rather than a different memorizing solution.
Output rescaling mainly changes feature-learning timescale after appropriate learning-rate treatment rather than optimization stability or effective loss geometry.
The polynomial teacher/committee machine preserves the mechanism relevant to modular arithmetic and real datasets.

techniques.role: Continuously tunes relative feature movement while holding architecture and initial weight norm fixed.
Measures whether initialization features emphasize task labels.
Compresses dynamics and test error to the mean vector and second-moment matrix.
Separates scale, target alignment, and spurious linear-mode errors.
Creates tasks with controlled initial feature difficulty.
Locates the intermediate regime where delayed but eventual generalization is possible.

evaluations.setting: Two-layer quadratic committee machine on high-dimensional Gaussian polynomial regression, vanilla full-batch GD, no weight decay.
evaluations.metric: Train/test MSE, feature moments, parameter norm, NTK alignment, exact error components, and time-to-grok.
evaluations.result: The model first approaches an initial-kernel predictor and later aligns its feature covariance to the teacher; alpha, epsilon, and sample size predict the delay regime.
evaluations.baseline: Frozen initialization-NTK regression and parameter sweeps.

evaluations.setting: Gaussian inputs labeled by descending eigenvectors of the initialization NTK.
evaluations.metric: CKA and train/test loss curves for high-, intermediate-, and low-eigenvalue labels.
evaluations.result: Top modes generalize immediately, very low modes do not generalize with the available data, and an intermediate mode groks.
evaluations.baseline: Different target eigenvectors under the same model/data distribution.

evaluations.setting: MNIST MLP, one-layer modular-addition transformer with AdamW/cross-entropy, modular-arithmetic MLP, and student-teacher networks.
evaluations.metric: Loss/accuracy timing while sweeping output scale or equivalent lazy parameterizations.
evaluations.result: Output scale continuously controls the observed delay and can make it vanish across these settings.
evaluations.baseline: Original grokking configurations and alternate alpha values.

limitations: The core exact decomposition is for a specially designed quadratic activation, Gaussian inputs, polynomial teacher, fixed positive readout weights, and full-batch GD.
No sharp theorem gives transition time, sample-size thresholds, or necessary and sufficient grokking conditions.
A finite-time departure from linearization is observed rather than rigorously derived from the network dynamics.
CKA is computed using test labels in the generic definition and therefore is a diagnostic, not generally an available training-time predictor.
Changing output scale can also change effective logits, gradients, calibration, optimization conditioning, and cross-entropy margins, especially in transformer experiments.
Broader experiments mostly show control of curve timing; they do not decompose features or causally verify the same mechanism.

The paper establishes one sufficient mechanism, while grokking is a phenotype that may also result from margin maximization, optimizer slingshots, circuit competition, embedding dynamics, or distribution shift.
failure_modes: The initial kernel is misaligned but the data are insufficient, so the network memorizes and never generalizes.
Alpha is too large and training remains permanently lazy at the inferior kernel solution.
Alpha is small enough that feature learning is immediate, eliminating delayed generalization even though final performance is good.
An adaptive optimizer or normalization cancels the intended scaling relationship between alpha and feature movement.
Low CKA arises from label noise or irrelevant tail modes that no learned representation can recover.
reusable_insights: Distinguish a delayed-generalization phenotype from any single proposed cause; demonstrate necessity with counterexamples and sufficiency with controlled models.
Tune feature-learning rate independently of initial parameter norm when testing lazy-versus-rich explanations.
Monitor NTK drift and task alignment alongside train/test loss to detect hidden representational progress after interpolation.
Search jointly over model-task alignment, learning timescale, and sample size rather than treating grokking as a one-hyperparameter effect.
Use loss rather than thresholded accuracy to avoid manufacturing abruptness through metric choice.
open_questions: What finite-width dynamics determine escape time from the lazy regime under GD, momentum, Adam, and weight decay?
Can training-only estimates of kernel-target alignment predict delayed generalization without test-label leakage?
Which grokking benchmarks are explained by feature-learning delay versus margin, circuit, embedding, or distributional mechanisms?
Can interventions that accelerate feature learning preserve the same final implicit bias and generalization?
How do width, depth, normalization, attention, and parameterization change the Goldilocks sample regime?

competitive_landscape.title: Grokking: Generalization Beyond Overfitting on Small Algorithmic Datasets
competitive_landscape.difference: Power et al. discovered delayed generalization in regularized transformer training on algorithmic data. The target paper broadens it to unregularized GD and proposes a feature-learning timescale mechanism.

competitive_landscape.title: Omnigrok: Grokking Beyond Algorithmic Data
competitive_landscape.difference: Omnigrok ties delayed generalization across datasets to initialization scale, weight decay, and representation learning. This paper argues scale matters because it induces lazy dynamics and gives increasing-norm, zero-decay counterexamples.

competitive_landscape.title: Explaining Grokking through Circuit Efficiency
competitive_landscape.difference: Varma et al. model competition between memorizing and generalizing circuits under regularization and efficiency. Lazy-to-rich dynamics instead locate the competition in fixed versus learned features and work without norm decrease, though both can coexist in modular arithmetic.

competitive_landscape.title: Grokking as a First Order Phase Transition in Two Layer Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Rubin et al. also frame grokking as beyond-lazy feature learning, using adaptive-kernel theory and a first-order phase-transition analogy in teacher-student models. The target paper emphasizes a continuous timescale delay controlled by output scale, alignment, and data size.

competitive_landscape.title: Mechanistic Insights into Grokking from the Embedding Layer
competitive_landscape.difference: This later work identifies rare-token update imbalance and bilinear embedding/downstream coupling as concrete modular-arithmetic bottlenecks. It refines the generic feature-learning story with architecture-specific dynamics not captured by an initialization NTK summary.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The authors claim delayed transition from lazy kernel fitting to rich feature learning is a general grokking mechanism controlled by output-scale laziness, initial NTK-target alignment, and an intermediate sample regime.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Sections 3-5 give zero-decay counterexamples and an exact toy loss decomposition; Section 6 and appendices sweep controls across MNIST, transformers, arithmetic, and student-teacher models.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: Concurrent work also linked grokking to feature learning and phase transitions, while earlier work emphasized norms, circuits, and optimizers. The strongest novelty is the clean unregularized polynomial construction, moment-level diagnosis, and separable alpha/alignment/data controls. It is a compelling sufficient mechanism, not a universal definition of grokking.

reviewer_notes: Read all 26 cached pages, including loss derivations, accuracy-metric critique, optimizer/weight-decay experiments, sample/alignment sweeps, and wider-model extensions. Primary arXiv/OpenReview predecessors and later embedding/phase-transition counterpoints were checked on 2026-08-23. Review treats the proposal as a mechanism that can cause grokking rather than the exclusive cause.
